doc: OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions. The dialect every other rule file may import: it is what a framework emits when it emits nothing of its own.

carriers.doc: The model's own output. One emission, so two tool calls in it are two calls whether or not the provider sent ids - a model asking twice looks exactly like this.
The completion, under the older convention name. Same fact, older spelling.
What this span produced, as an event. On a generation span this is the model's own emission.
A span's own record of a tool it ran: one emission it produced.

One emission too, but received: the framework handing a past result back to a model. Its time is the hand-back, and it is input to whatever the span then produces. Reading it as output made a re-sent result look like a generation's own answer.
A re-sent turn: history by definition.
A system turn inside the conversation stream. Deliberately not a detached request frame: an event in a stream is in-band and may be a turn, framed by its position.
The awkward one: a replay for most frameworks, and the actual output for a choiceless generation span. Read as a snapshot here; direction is decided downstream.
The prompt, under the older convention name.
The conversation as this span received it, as an event.
What this span produced, in one payload. Ordered, its own, and two of anything in it are two - the attribute form of gen_ai.choice. Being an emission is what keeps a response's parts together.
The family's root: the array itself, which expands into one observation per message. A key *beneath* it is one message's own member and stays whole.
What this span received: a conversation as it saw it, which may re-state earlier turns.
The family's root: the array itself, which expands into one observation per message. A key *beneath* it is one message's own member and stays whole.

The system prompt a model was given, reported beside the conversation rather than inside it. A detached request frame: it asserts 'this precedes every other input of the request that carried me', which is a constraint rather than a position.
A tool span's own result under the current conventions. One emission - a tool is called once.
The arguments that tool span was handed: the same pair, differing only in direction. The clearest case for direction being its own fact rather than something inferred from shape.
The deprecated indexed request family. Received, like the current spelling.
The deprecated indexed response family.
Anything else under the current request namespace: received by definition.
Anything else under the current response namespace: produced by definition.

messages.doc: The request as an indexed attribute family - `gen_ai.prompt.0.role`, `.0.content`, `.1.role`. A list of objects flattened into dotted keys because OTel attributes are a flat map. `content` is required because an index exists as soon as any key mentions it, and the family also holds keys that are not turns.
The response in the same encoding.
The system prompt as a parts array. Wrapped with the parts under `parts` rather than `content`, which is how the conventions write a structured instruction.
The request, stored as it arrived: normalisation happens at query time, so the payload is kept whole.
The response, stored as it arrived.
A whole conversation reported on an agent-run span. Wrapped as context with a literal naming what it is, so the array normalises as history rather than as one turn's content.

A tool call. Built as a `tool_use` block, not a bare object under a role: the block shape is what carries the name and the id through normalisation, and the id is what lets the result be paired with this call rather than guessed at by content. The name falls back to the span name because the conventions prescribe `execute_tool {name}` there, and it defaults to empty rather than being omitted - a block whose shape requires a name carries an empty one, and the two are different values to anything hashing the payload.
The answer to it, as a `tool_result` block carrying the same id. Here the name is *omitted* when absent rather than defaulted, which is what the extractor did - the block is identified by its id.

span_facts.doc: The convention's own statement, and the pair of attributes that only appear together on a call being run.

signals.doc: The operation the span reports performing.
A tool name *and* a call id. The name alone sits on a model span that merely mentions a tool; with an id it is a call being run.
